1	# Product Requirements Document - autom9
2	
3	**Author:** CodeBeard  
4	 **Date:** 2026-04-08
5	
6	## Executive Summary
7	
8	autom9 is a Tableau dashboard extension that embeds an AI agent directly into the planning tool consultants already use as their system of record.
9	The agent enables consultants to complete planning workflows — submitting Smartsheet requests, creating Google Calendar invites, picking up open  
10	 work — without leaving Tableau. The core insight: the problem is not data visibility, which Tableau already solves, but the broken link between  
11	 seeing data and acting on it. Every alternative requires pulling data out of context; autom9 closes that loop inside the tool.
12	
13	The POC targets ~80 consultants at a professional services firm. The underlying platform — BYOM (OpenAI and Anthropic), JSON-configured workflows,
14	no external automation dependency — is designed to support multiple agent use cases beyond the initial planning assistant. The POC proves the  
15	 value of the first use case and the extensibility of the platform simultaneously.
16	
17	### What Makes This Special
18	
19	**Workflow completion in a single surface.** Tableau is where consultants review their planning data; autom9 is where they act on it — same tab,  
20	 same context, no handoff to Slack, Smartsheet, or email. This is architecturally only possible as a native Tableau Extension.
21	
22	**BYOM + JSON-driven extensibility.** New agent workflows are added via configuration, not bespoke engineering. The platform is explicitly  
23	 designed  
24	 to support a growing library of agent workflows. This directly counters Salesforce Einstein's model-locked, CRM-centric approach to AI in Tableau.
25	
26	**No direct competitor.** No commercially available Tableau extension offers BYOM agentic workflows with external tool integration. The  
27	 competitive window is estimated at 12–18 months before Salesforce closes it with a native Agentforce integration.
28	
29	                                                                          |
30	
31	------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------  
32	 **Project Type** | B2B SaaS / Platform  
33	 **Domain** | AI / Workflow Automation  
34	 **Complexity** | Medium  
35	 **Project Context** | Greenfield
36	
37	## Success Criteria
38	
39	### User Success
40	
41	• **Primary metric:** 60%+ of the 80 POC consultants complete at least one Smartsheet planning request via the extension per week within 60 days  
42	 of launch. Google Calendar invite creation is tracked but optional for this threshold.  
43	 • **Qualitative signal:** Testimonials from consultants citing measurable reduction in time spent on scheduling logistics and fewer context  
44	 switches across tools.
45	
46	### Business Success
47	
48	• POC demonstrates genuine, repeatable value for the target user group — evidenced by adoption rate and qualitative feedback.  
49	 • Platform extensibility validated internally by configuring and deploying at least one additional agent workflow via the JSON system (post-POC,  
50	 not a v1 deliverable).
51	
52	### Technical Success
53	
54	• All agent interactions logged with sufficient detail to diagnose issues, trace failed tool calls, and identify latency patterns.  
55	 • Agent responses complete within 20 seconds during the POC phase (nice-to-have; no hard SLA in v1).  
56	 • Extension architecture supports future air-gapped deployment — local LLM integration and fully local install. Design constraint for v1, not a v1
57	deliverable.
58	
59	### Measurable Outcomes
60	
61	| Metric                                      | Target                     | Timeframe           |
62	| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------- |
63	| Weekly active users (workflow completion)   | 60%+ of 80 consultants     | 60 days post-launch |
64	| Smartsheet requests submitted via extension | Tracked per user           | Ongoing             |
65	| Agent response time (p95)                   | ≤20 seconds (nice-to-have) | POC phase           |
66	| Failed/errored agent interactions           | Logged and reviewable      | At launch           |
67	
68	## Product Scope
69	
70	### MVP — Minimum Viable Product
71	
72	• Consultant planning view: open days surfaced from Snowflake via Tableau data source  
73	 • Task ingestion from individual Google Docs with clarifying Q&A in the chat panel  
74	 • Smartsheet planning request trigger from the extension  
75	 • Google Calendar invite creation around existing engagements  
76	 • Org-wide open work board (Google Doc) with billable/internal priority logic, availability check, accept/decline flow, and coordinator  
77	 notification  
78	 • BYOM: OpenAI and Anthropic support  
79	 • JSON workflow configuration system (versionable)  
80	 • Agent interaction logging (admin diagnostics)  
81	 • Integration status check on extension load  
82	 • Token-based data masking before LLM calls + rehydration after response  
83	 • Extension install: Tableau Desktop (development) + Tableau Cloud/Server (production)
84	
85	### Growth Features (Post-MVP)
86	
87	• Per-user data scoping (agent limited to authenticated consultant's own records)  
88	 • Group-level credential management  
89	 • Licensing mechanism: license key in .trex file validated against registered Tableau URL  
90	 • Slack integration: surface open work requests from emoji-tagged messages  
91	 • At least one additional agent workflow configured via JSON (platform extensibility validation)  
92	 • Expanded logging and analytics: adoption dashboards, workflow completion rates  
93	 • Additional BYOM model support
94	
95	### Vision (Future)
96	
97	• Self-hosted premium tier: customer-managed infrastructure, no external data dependency  
98	 • Local LLM support for air-gapped environments  
99	 • Open marketplace of Tableau agent workflows  
100	 • Manager/team-level views across multiple consultants  
101	 • Consulting Accelerator: packaged product for professional services firms
102	
103	## User Journeys
104	
105	### Journey 1: Consultant — Planning Request (Happy Path)
106	
107	**Meet Priya.** She's a consultant three weeks into a new engagement, with two open days next week and a task list she's been meaning to work  
108	 through. It's Monday morning, and she opens the Planning dashboard in Tableau — the same place she always starts her week. On the right side of  
109	 the screen, the autom9 panel is waiting.
110	
111	She clicks into the chat. The agent already knows her open days from the Tableau data source — it surfaces them without her having to ask. It's  
112	 also read her Google Doc task list and has two questions: one project has a kick-off she said was flexible — is next Thursday still okay? And  
113	 there's a client deliverable she flagged as urgent — does she want to block time around it?
114	
115	She answers both questions in plain language. The agent submits the Smartsheet planning request and creates the Google Calendar invites around her
116	existing commitments. The whole interaction took four minutes. She didn't open Slack, navigate to Smartsheet, or toggle between tabs.
117	
118	**Requirements revealed:** Snowflake/Tableau data read, Google Docs ingestion, clarifying Q&A in chat, Smartsheet integration, Google Calendar  
119	 integration, session context retention.
120	
121	---
122	
123	### Journey 2: Consultant — Open Work Opportunity
124	
125	**Meet James.** He has three open days next week and no pending task list items. He opens his Planning dashboard and the autom9 panel surfaces  
126	 open work opportunities — billable client requests first, then internal projects. The agent doesn't mix the two without making the distinction  
127	 clear.
128	
129	Before presenting an opportunity, the agent checks James's availability against the commitment requested. A client team needs someone for a two-  
130	 day  
131	 workshop. The agent reads his open days from Snowflake, applies a 5% buffer to the time estimate, and confirms he can credibly commit — flagging  
132	 the constraint if he can't cover the full ask plus buffer.
133	
134	The agent asks: is he the right fit, and is he willing to contribute? James reads the brief from the org-wide Google Doc and says yes. The agent  
135	 logs his interest and flags the coordinator. If James declines, the agent acknowledges it, logs the decision, and does not resurface the same  
136	 opportunity.
137	
138	**Requirements revealed:** Org-wide Google Doc read (billable + internal, typed separately), priority logic (billable > internal), availability +
139	buffer calculation (open days vs. time requested + 5%), accept/decline flow, coordinator notification, open work board write-back.
140	
141	---
142	
143	### Journey 3: Admin / Configurator — Extension Setup
144	
145	**Meet the person who makes this work before Priya and James ever open it.** An ops lead or internal tools developer. Their job: install autom9 on
146	Tableau Cloud, connect it to the right data sources, and configure the consultant planning workflow.
147	
148	They install the extension via the Tableau extension gallery (or a local .trex file for development). They configure BYOM credentials — an  
149	 Anthropic API key to start — and load the JSON workflow config file defining the available tools (Snowflake read, Google Docs read, Smartsheet  
150	 write, Calendar write) and agent instructions. They test the Snowflake connection, confirm the agent responds correctly, verify the interaction is
151	logged, and mark the workflow active.
152	
153	When a Google OAuth token expires two weeks later, they open the logs. The failed tool call is there with enough context to diagnose. They refresh
154	the token, retest, done.
155	
156	**Requirements revealed:** Extension install (Tableau Desktop + Cloud), BYOM credential configuration, JSON workflow loader, tool connection  
157	 testing, admin logging interface, OAuth/credential management.
158	
159	---
160	
161	### Journey Requirements Summary
162	
163	| Capability Area                                                | Revealed By  |
164	| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
165	| Snowflake/Tableau data read                                    | Journey 1, 3 |
166	| Google Docs ingestion (individual + org-wide)                  | Journey 1, 2 |
167	| Clarifying Q&A in chat panel                                   | Journey 1    |
168	| Smartsheet planning request                                    | Journey 1    |
169	| Google Calendar invite creation                                | Journey 1    |
170	| Open work matching + priority logic (billable > internal)      | Journey 2    |
171	| Availability + buffer calculation (open days vs. request + 5%) | Journey 2    |
172	| Accept/decline flow + coordinator notification                 | Journey 2    |
173	| BYOM credential configuration                                  | Journey 3    |
174	| JSON workflow configuration loader                             | Journey 3    |
175	| Agent interaction logging + admin diagnostics                  | Journey 3    |
176	| Extension install (Tableau Desktop + Cloud)                    | Journey 3    |
177	
178	## Domain-Specific Requirements
179	
180	### Data Access & Privacy
181	
182	• The agent reads org-wide planning data in v1. Per-user data scoping is deferred to v2.  
183	 • Consultant planning data (names, client assignments, engagement details, open days) must not be transmitted to external LLM providers in  
184	 identifiable form.  
185	 • **Data masking pattern:** Before any LLM call, the agent replaces identifiable fields with opaque tokens (e.g. CLIENT_A, ENGAGEMENT_001,  
186	 CONSULTANT_X). A token map is held in memory for the session. On receiving the LLM response, real values are rehydrated from the token map before
187	output is displayed or tool actions are executed. The LLM never sees real names or client identifiers. This applies to all LLM calls regardless of
188	BYOM provider.
189	
190	### Credential Management
191	
192	• Integration credentials (Google OAuth, Smartsheet API key, Snowflake connection) are stored at the org level for v1. Group-level scoping is a v2
193	consideration.  
194	 • Credentials are never exposed in logs, config files, or the chat interface.
195	
196	### Integration Reliability
197	
198	• On extension load, a status check runs against all configured integrations (Snowflake, Google Docs, Smartsheet, Google Calendar, LLM provider).
199	Unavailable services are surfaced to the consultant before any interaction begins.  
200	 • Integration failures during a workflow result in a graceful, specific error message. No partial execution of dependent actions.  
201	 • Status check results are logged for admin diagnostics.
202	
203	### Risk Mitigations
204	
205	| Risk                             | Mitigation                                                        |
206	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
207	| Real data transmitted to LLM     | Token-based masking before LLM call; rehydration after response   |
208	| Credential exposure              | Org-level encrypted storage; never surfaced in UI or logs         |
209	| Mid-workflow integration failure | Graceful failure with clear messaging; no partial execution       |
210	| Overly broad data access         | Per-user scoping deferred to v2; org-wide read acceptable for POC |
211	
212	## Innovation & Novel Patterns
213	
214	### Detected Innovation Areas
215	
216	**1. Embedded agentic AI in a BI tool.**  
217	 autom9 is the first commercially available Tableau extension to offer BYOM agentic workflows with external tool integration. The innovation is not
218	just the AI agent — it's embedding it _inside_ the BI tool. Tableau's Extensions API allows third-party panels to render within the dashboard  
219	 surface and read the underlying data context. No existing product combines this with LLM orchestration and multi-tool action execution.
220	
221	**2. BYOM in an enterprise BI context.**  
222	 Salesforce Einstein and Tableau Pulse lock users into Salesforce's model stack. autom9's BYOM architecture — OpenAI and Anthropic from day one,  
223	 local model compatibility planned — directly counter-positions against model-lock that enterprise teams are pushing back on. This proposition does
224	not exist in the current Tableau ecosystem.
225	
226	**3. JSON-driven workflow configuration as the extension mechanism.**  
227	 New agent use-cases are configuration, not software releases. This pattern unlocks the marketplace thesis: a third-party developer can ship a new
228	Tableau agent workflow without touching the core platform. No comparable pattern exists in the Tableau extension ecosystem today.
229	
230	**4. Token-based data masking for LLM privacy in enterprise workflows.**  
231	 Masking identifiable data before LLM calls and rehydrating after avoids the typical tradeoff of either exposing data to the model or degrading  
232	 reasoning quality. An emerging pattern in enterprise AI; not yet standard in embedded BI tooling.
233	
234	### Market Context & Competitive Landscape
235	
236	• **Tableau native AI (Einstein, Pulse):** Reactive Q&A only. Cloud-only, model-locked, no external tool integration, no workflow execution.  
237	 • **n8n / Zapier + Tableau connectors:** External automation requiring data to leave Tableau context. No embedded experience.  
238	 • **Standalone AI planning tools:** Require separate login, data sync, and context-switching — the exact problem autom9 eliminates.  
239	 • **Estimated competitive window:** 12–18 months before Salesforce's Agentforce-in-Tableau integration arrives. It will be CRM-centric and model-
240	locked by design.
241	
242	### Validation Approach
243	
244	• **POC as proof:** Adoption rate and qualitative feedback from 80 consultants validate that embedded agentic workflows create genuine value.  
245	 • **Extensibility proof:** At least one additional JSON-configured workflow during or after the POC validates the platform thesis without a full  
246	 product release.  
247	 • **BYOM proof:** Swapping between OpenAI and Anthropic via config change validates the BYOM architecture is real, not aspirational.
248	
249	### Innovation Risks
250	
251	| Risk                                                            | Mitigation                                                              |
252	| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
253	| Tableau Extensions API limitations constrain agent capabilities | Prototype against API limits early; scope POC to demonstrably supported |
254	| capabilities                                                    |
255	| Token masking degrades LLM reasoning quality                    | Validate masking/rehydration accuracy in testing; tune token scheme for |
256	| semantic coherence                                              |
257	| JSON workflow system proves too rigid                           | Validate with a second workflow during POC; adjust schema before v2     |
258	| Salesforce closes competitive window faster than expected       | Speed to a loved, adopted POC is the strategic priority                 |
259	
260	## B2B SaaS Specific Requirements
261	
262	### Tenancy Model
263	
264	| Delivery Model                                              | Description                                                   | Target Customer                          |
265	| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
266	| **Cloud (Shared Backend)**                                  | Customer firm is a tenant on autom9's shared infrastructure.  | Standard subscription customers          |
267	| Isolated data, credentials, and workflow config per tenant. |
268	| **Self-Hosted (Premium)**                                   | Full autom9 stack deployed within customer infrastructure. No | Privacy-conscious enterprises; regulated |
269	| external data dependency. Requires local LLM.               | industries                                                    |
270	
271	**POC context:** Single-tenant installation within one firm's Tableau environment. Tenancy architecture is a v2+ concern; v1 must not preclude  
272	 either model.
273	
274	### Permission Model
275	
276	| Role                                 | Capabilities                                                                                                        |
277	| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
278	| **Admin / Configurator**             | Install extension; configure BYOM credentials (org-level); load and update JSON workflow config; access interaction |
279	| logs; manage integration connections |
280	| **Consultant (User)**                | Interact with agent via chat panel; complete planning workflows; accept/decline open work opportunities             |
281	
282	No additional permission distinctions in v1. LLM provider selection is admin-controlled.
283	
284	### Integration Map
285	
286	| Integration              | Direction | Purpose                               |
287	| ------------------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------- |
288	| Snowflake (via Tableau)  | Read      | Consultant planning data, open days   |
289	| Google Docs (individual) | Read      | Consultant task list                  |
290	| Google Docs (org-wide)   | Read      | Open work board (billable + internal) |
291	| Smartsheet               | Write     | Planning request submission           |
292	| Google Calendar          | Write     | Calendar invite creation              |
293	| OpenAI API               | Outbound  | LLM inference (BYOM option 1)         |
294	| Anthropic API            | Outbound  | LLM inference (BYOM option 2)         |
295	
296	### Implementation Considerations
297	
298	• Distributed as a .trex file for Tableau Desktop; registered in Tableau Cloud/Server for production.  
299	 • JSON workflow config must be versionable — config updates must not break in-flight sessions.  
300	 • Tenant isolation in the shared backend model requires credentials, workflow configs, and logs scoped strictly per tenant.
301	
302	## Scoping Philosophy & Risk Strategy
303	
304	### MVP Philosophy
305	
306	**POC-first.** The goal is validated learning with a captive user group, not market launch. The minimum viable proof is a consultant completing a
307	Smartsheet planning request without leaving Tableau. The open work journey (Journey 2) adds POC value but is the first candidate for deferral if  
308	 resources compress.
309	
310	### Risk Mitigation Strategy
311	
312	**Technical Risks:**
313	
314	• Token masking + rehydration is the most novel and least proven element — prototype it first. If it degrades LLM reasoning quality, the agent may
315	misfire on tool calls or ask poor clarifying questions.  
316	 • Validate Tableau Extensions API capabilities (data read, panel rendering, session persistence) before committing to the full feature set.
317	
318	**Market Risks:**
319	
320	• 60-day adoption target is the primary validation signal. If adoption lags, qualitative interviews identify whether the issue is UX, workflow fit,
321	or discoverability.
322	
323	**Resource Risks:**
324	
325	• Journey 2 (open work) is the first deferral candidate. Journey 1 (planning request) is the core proof.
326	
327	## Functional Requirements
328	
329	### Planning Data & Availability
330	
331	• **FR1:** Consultant can view their open days and scheduled engagements sourced from Snowflake via the Tableau data source within the extension  
332	 panel  
333	 • **FR2:** Consultant can view their task list ingested from their designated individual Google Doc
334	
335	### Agent Interaction & Workflow Execution
336	
337	• **FR3:** Consultant can interact with the AI agent via a chat interface embedded in the Tableau extension panel  
338	 • **FR4:** Agent can ask clarifying questions about task timing, priority, and scheduling preferences before taking action  
339	 • **FR5:** Agent retains context within a session to support multi-turn clarifying conversations  
340	 • **FR6:** Consultant can review the agent's proposed actions before execution is confirmed
341	
342	### Open Work Discovery & Matching
343	
344	• **FR7:** Agent surfaces open work opportunities from the org-wide Google Doc, distinguishing billable client work from internal projects  
345	 • **FR8:** Agent prioritises billable opportunities above internal project opportunities  
346	 • **FR9:** Agent calculates whether a consultant's available capacity meets the time commitment of an open work opportunity, including a 5% buffer
347	• **FR10:** Consultant can accept or decline an open work opportunity from within the extension panel  
348	 • **FR11:** Agent notifies the relevant coordinator when a consultant accepts an open work opportunity  
349	 • **FR12:** Agent does not resurface a previously declined opportunity to the same consultant
350	
351	### Integration & Tool Actions
352	
353	• **FR13:** Agent submits a Smartsheet planning request on behalf of the consultant  
354	 • **FR14:** Agent creates Google Calendar invites for the consultant around existing engagements  
355	 • **FR15:** Extension checks connectivity to all configured integrations on load and surfaces any unavailable services before interaction begins  
356	 • **FR16:** Agent fails gracefully with a specific error message if an integration becomes unavailable during a workflow, without partially  
357	 executing dependent actions
358	
359	### Data Privacy & Security
360	
361	• **FR17:** Agent masks identifiable data fields (names, client identifiers, engagement IDs) with opaque tokens before transmitting any context to
362	the LLM provider  
363	 • **FR18:** Agent rehydrates masked tokens with real values from the session token map before displaying output or executing tool actions  
364	 • **FR19:** Integration credentials are never exposed in logs, the chat interface, or configuration files visible to consultants
365	
366	### Extension Configuration & Administration
367	
368	• **FR20:** Admin can install and register the extension in Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server  
369	 • **FR21:** Admin can configure the BYOM LLM provider and API credentials at the org level via the extension configuration panel  
370	 • **FR22:** Admin can load and update the JSON workflow configuration file defining agent capabilities, tool access, and workflow parameters  
371	 • **FR23:** Admin can test integration connections from the configuration panel before activating the extension for consultants  
372	 • **FR24:** Admin can access agent interaction logs with sufficient detail to diagnose failed tool calls, error patterns, and latency  
373	 • **FR25:** Integration status check results are logged for admin review
374	
375	### Platform & Extensibility
376	
377	• **FR26:** New agent workflows can be added by updating the JSON workflow configuration file without modifying platform code  
378	 • **FR27:** The JSON workflow configuration defines available tools, agent instructions, and workflow parameters in a versionable format  
379	 • **FR28:** The extension supports OpenAI and Anthropic as BYOM LLM providers, switchable via configuration change  
380	 • **FR29:** The extension is compatible with Tableau Desktop and Tableau Cloud/Server
381	
382	## Non-Functional Requirements
383	
384	### Performance
385	
386	• **NFR1:** Agent responses complete within 20 seconds (p95) under normal operating conditions during the POC phase. Nice-to-have target; no hard
387	SLA in v1.  
388	 • **NFR2:** The extension panel renders and integration status check completes within 5 seconds of Tableau dashboard load.  
389	 • **NFR3:** The chat interface displays a visible processing indicator within 1 second of the consultant submitting a message.
390	
391	### Security
392	
393	• **NFR4:** All data transmitted between the extension and external services (LLM providers, Snowflake, Google, Smartsheet) is encrypted in  
394	 transit (TLS 1.2+).  
395	 • **NFR5:** API credentials and integration tokens are stored encrypted at rest and never surfaced in logs, UI elements, or configuration files  
396	 accessible to consultants.  
397	 • **NFR6:** The token masking system transmits no real consultant names, client identifiers, or engagement IDs to any external LLM provider under
398	any circumstances.  
399	 • **NFR7:** Agent interaction logs capture only masked data representations — no raw LLM payloads containing identifiable fields.
400	
401	### Integration Reliability
402	
403	• **NFR8:** The extension identifies and reports unavailability of any configured integration within the 5-second load status check window.  
404	 • **NFR9:** A failure in one integration does not cascade to prevent other integrations from functioning.  
405	 • **NFR10:** The JSON workflow configuration system handles version mismatches gracefully — a config update does not break or corrupt an in-flight
406	session.
407	
408	### Scalability
409	
410	• **NFR11:** The extension supports concurrent usage by all 80 POC consultants without degradation in agent response time.  
411	 • **NFR12:** The platform architecture imposes no design constraints that would prevent future multi-tenant isolation (cloud shared backend), even
412	if not implemented in v1.

1	# autom9-backend
2	
3	FastAPI backend for the autom9 Tableau extension. Handles admin configuration, BYOM LLM credential management, workflow config, integration health checks, and session tracking.
4	
5	## What it does
6	
7	autom9 is a Tableau extension that lets consultants interact with an AI agent for planning workflows — submitting Smartsheet requests, creating Google Calendar invites, and surfacing open work opportunities — without leaving Tableau.
8	
9	This backend serves:
10	- **Admin API** — BYOM credential setup (OpenAI/Anthropic), JSON workflow config upload
11	- **Status API** — parallel integration health checks on extension load
12	- **Session API** — session creation tied to Tableau user context
13	- **Config API** — public endpoint the extension fetches on load to get active workflow tools/instructions
14	
15	## Tech stack
16	
17	- Python 3.11+ with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
18	- FastAPI + Uvicorn (async)
19	- SQLAlchemy 2.0 async ORM + asyncpg + PostgreSQL
20	- Alembic migrations
21	- Pydantic v2 + pydantic-settings
22	- Fernet symmetric encryption (credentials at rest)
23	- pytest + pytest-asyncio (real DB, savepoint-based test isolation)
24

1	# autom9-extension
2	
3	Tableau dashboard extension frontend for autom9. Built with Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite. Loads inside Tableau Desktop or Tableau Cloud, initialises a backend session, checks integration health, and (in later epics) surfaces an AI planning agent for consultants.
4	
5	## What it does
6	
7	On load, the extension:
8	1. Calls `tableau.extensions.initializeAsync()` — waits for the Tableau runtime before doing anything
9	2. Creates a backend session (`POST /api/sessions`) tied to the Tableau user identity
10	3. Runs parallel integration health checks (`GET /api/status`) and displays results in `StatusBar`
11	4. Renders the admin panel (`AdminConfig`) when the URL contains `?admin`
12	
13	Admin panel lets an admin:
14	- Select a BYOM LLM provider (OpenAI / Anthropic) and paste an API key → `POST /api/admin/credentials`
15	- Paste a JSON workflow config and upload it → `POST /api/admin/config`
16	
17	## Tech stack
18	
19	- [Svelte 5](https://svelte.dev/) with runes (`$state()`) — no legacy store API
20	- TypeScript (strict)
21	- Vite 8
22	- `@tableau/extensions-api-types` for Tableau runtime types
23	
24	## Project structure
25	
26	```
27	src/
28	  main.ts                        # Mounts App into #app
29	  App.svelte                     # Root: Tableau init gate, session creation, status fetch
30	  app.css                        # Global styles
31	  lib/
32	    api.ts                       # apiFetch() — typed HTTP client, 10s timeout, ApiError on failure
33	    tableau.ts                   # initializeExtension() + getTableauUserId() wrappers
34	  stores/
35	    session.svelte.ts            # sessionStore — holds session_id + tableau_user_id
36	    status.svelte.ts             # statusStore — holds integration health results
37	  components/
38	    StatusBar.svelte             # Renders per-integration health indicators
39	    AdminConfig.svelte           # BYOM credential form (onMount fetches existing masked key)
40	    WorkflowConfigPanel.svelte   # JSON config textarea → POST /api/admin/config
41	autom9.trex                      # Tableau extension manifest (source URL, permissions)
42	```
43	
44	## The `.trex` manifest
45	
46	`autom9.trex` is the Tableau extension manifest. Register it in Tableau Desktop via **Dashboard → Extensions → My Extensions**.
47	
48	- `<source-location>` points to `http://localhost:5173` for dev (Vite dev server)
49	- For production, update this URL to wherever the built extension is hosted
50	- `min-api-version` is `1.4` — compatible with Tableau Desktop 2019.2+ and Tableau Cloud
51	
52	## Environment variables
53	
54	| Variable | Default | Description |
55	|---|---|---|
56	| `VITE_BACKEND_URL` | `http://localhost:8000` | Backend base URL — overridden for staging/production builds |
57	
58	Set in a `.env` file at the project root:
59	
60	```
61	VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8000
62	```
63	
64	## Running locally
65	
66	```bash
67	# Install dependencies
68	npm install
69	
70	# Start dev server (http://localhost:5173)
71	npm run dev
72	```
73	
74	Register `autom9.trex` in Tableau Desktop to load the extension in a dashboard. Without Tableau, the extension shell still renders — `lib/tableau.ts` falls back gracefully when no Tableau runtime is present.
75	
76	## Building
77	
78	```bash
79	npm run build       # outputs to dist/
80	npm run check       # TypeScript type-check (svelte-check + tsc)
81	```
82	
83	## apiFetch conventions
84	
85	All backend calls go through `apiFetch()` in `src/lib/api.ts`:
86	
87	- **Timeout:** 10 seconds — throws `ApiError("REQUEST_TIMEOUT", ...)` on abort
88	- **Errors:** non-2xx responses parse `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}` from the backend envelope and throw `ApiError(code, message, status)`
89	- **Network failure:** throws `ApiError("NETWORK_ERROR", ...)`
90	- `Content-Type: application/json` is set by default; override in `init.headers`
91	
92	Admin routes require `X-Autom9-Token` — pass it in `init.headers`. The frontend does not inject it automatically (v1 dev-time concern; the token is never stored in the browser).
93	
94	## Admin panel
95	
96	Access via `?admin` (or `?admin=1`) in the extension URL. The backend `X-Autom9-Token` header must be provided by the caller — the UI has no login form.
97	
98	The admin panel has two sections:
99	- **BYOM Credential Setup** (`AdminConfig.svelte`) — provider select + API key input. On mount, fetches the current masked key state to indicate whether credentials already exist.
100	- **Workflow Configuration** (`WorkflowConfigPanel.svelte`) — textarea for the JSON workflow config. Client-side JSON parse before sending gives immediate feedback on malformed input.
101	
102	## What's not built yet
103	
104	| Component | Story |
105	|---|---|
106	| `DataPanel.svelte` — open days + task list from Tableau/Google Docs | Epic 3, Story 3.1 |
107	| `ChatPanel.svelte`, `MessageList.svelte`, `InputBar.svelte` — agent chat | Epic 3, Story 3.3 |
108	| `ActionConfirm.svelte` — pre-execution action confirmation | Epic 3, Story 3.4 |
109	| `chatStore` state machine | Epic 3, Story 3.3 |
110	| Open work board display | Epic 4, Story 4.1 |

2	Token masking and rehydration pipeline for the autom9 agent.
3	
4	This module is the ONLY place where PII masking/rehydration logic lives.
5	It must NEVER be inlined in orchestration code.
6	
7	ARC-9: 100% branch coverage is a hard acceptance gate for this file.
8	"""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	
12	class MaskingError(Exception):
13	    """Raised when masking is attempted on invalid input."""
14	
15	
16	# Category → token prefix mapping.
17	# "generic" is intentionally absent — it hits the .get() default branch ("VALUE").
18	_CATEGORY_PREFIXES: dict[str, str] = {
19	    "consultant": "CONSULTANT",
20	    "client": "CLIENT",
21	    "engagement": "ENGAGEMENT",
22	}
23	
24	
25	class TokenMap:
26	    """Session-scoped bidirectional mapping of opaque tokens ↔ real values.
27	
28	    Lifecycle: created at session start, reset on every extension load.
29	    Never persisted to any storage — in-memory only.
30	    Thread-safe for single-process async use (Python GIL + no concurrent writes).
31	    """
32	
33	    def __init__(self) -> None:
34	        self._token_to_real: dict[str, str] = {}
35	        self._real_to_token: dict[str, str] = {}
36	        self._counters: dict[str, int] = {}
37	
38	    def register(self, real_value: str, category: str = "generic") -> str:
39	        """Return the opaque token for *real_value*, registering it if not yet seen.
40	
41	        Idempotent: the same real value always maps to the same token within a session.
42	        Raises MaskingError if *real_value* is empty.
43	        """
44	        if not real_value or not real_value.strip():
45	            raise MaskingError("Cannot mask empty value")
46	        if real_value in self._real_to_token:
47	            return self._real_to_token[real_value]
48	        prefix = _CATEGORY_PREFIXES.get(category, "VALUE")
49	        count = self._counters.get(prefix, 0) + 1
50	        self._counters[prefix] = count
51	        token = f"{prefix}_{count:03d}"
52	        self._token_to_real[token] = real_value
53	        self._real_to_token[real_value] = token
54	        return token
55	
56	    def rehydrate(self, text: str) -> str:
57	        """Replace all known tokens in *text* with their real values.
58	
59	        Returns *text* unchanged if empty or if no tokens are present.
60	        """
61	        if not text:
62	            return text
63	        result = text
64	        for token, real in self._token_to_real.items():
65	            result = result.replace(token, real)
66	        return result
67	
68	    def reset(self) -> None:
69	        """Clear all mappings. Called at session end / extension reload."""
70	        self._token_to_real.clear()
71	        self._real_to_token.clear()
72	        self._counters.clear()
73	
74	    @property
75	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
76	        """True if no values have been registered yet."""
77	        return not bool(self._token_to_real)
78

80	def _infer_category(field_name: str) -> str:
81	    """Infer the masking category from a field name (case-insensitive substring match).
82	
83	    Rules (first match wins):
84	    - "consultant" in name → "consultant"
85	    - "client" in name     → "client"
86	    - "engagement" in name → "engagement"
87	    - otherwise            → "generic"
88	    """
89	    lower = field_name.lower()
90	    if "consultant" in lower:
91	        return "consultant"
92	    if "client" in lower:
93	        return "client"
94	    if "engagement" in lower:
95	        return "engagement"
96	    return "generic"

99	def mask_fields(fields: dict[str, str], token_map: TokenMap) -> dict[str, str]:
100	    """Mask a dict of {field_name: real_value} pairs.
101	
102	    Category is inferred from the field name via `_infer_category`.
103	    Returns a new dict with the same keys and token values.
104	    Empty *fields* dict → returns empty dict.
105	    """
106	    return {
107	        field_name: token_map.register(real_value, _infer_category(field_name))
108	        for field_name, real_value in fields.items()
109	    }

112	def mask_text(text: str, token_map: TokenMap) -> str:
113	    """Replace any registered real values that appear in *text* with their tokens.
114	
115	    Applies longest-match-first to prevent partial substitutions
116	    (e.g. "Acme Corp" masked before "Acme" if both are registered).
117	    Returns *text* unchanged if empty.
118	    """
119	    if not text:
120	        return text
121	    result = text
122	    for real, token in sorted(token_map._real_to_token.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[0])):
123	        result = result.replace(real, token)

131	    rather than calling `token_map.rehydrate` directly, so all rehydration flows
132	    through the same entry point for future auditing.
133	    """

33	        updated, leaving the previous active config intact (NFR10 rollback safety).

## Comprehensive Architecture Overview: autom9

### 1. **Project Purpose**

**autom9** is a Tableau dashboard extension that embeds an AI agent directly into the planning tool consultants already use. The agent enables consultants to complete planning workflows—submitting Smartsheet requests, creating Google Calendar invites, and discovering open work opportunities—without leaving Tableau.

**Core innovation:** The extension eliminates context-switching by keeping the agent inside the BI tool (Tableau), where planning data already lives. The product targets ~80 consultants at a professional services firm and is designed with extensibility for future agent workflows through JSON configuration (not code changes).

---

### 2. **High-Level Architecture**

The system is a **two-tier architecture**:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  FRONTEND: Tableau Extension (Svelte 5 + TypeScript)   │
│  Location: autom9-extension/                            │
│  Runs inside: Tableau Desktop / Tableau Cloud           │
└────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
         HTTP (CORS + API)
                 │
┌────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  BACKEND: FastAPI Service (Python 3.11+)                │
│  Location: autom9-backend/                              │
│  Storage: PostgreSQL + Alembic migrations               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flows:**
- Extension initializes on Tableau load → creates backend session
- Extension runs parallel integration health checks → displays status
- Admin (via `?admin` URL param) configures BYOM credentials and workflow JSON
- Consultant sends chat message → backend masks PII → calls LLM → rehydrates → returns response
- Agent orchestrates tool execution (Smartsheet, Google Calendar, etc.) through integration registry

---

### 3. **Key Modules & Responsibilities**

#### **Frontend (autom9-extension)**

| Module | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| **`App.svelte`** | Root component: Tableau runtime gate, session creation, error boundary |
| **`stores/session.svelte.ts`** | Session state (session_id, tableau_user_id) + in-memory token map for masking |
| **`stores/status.svelte.ts`** | Integration health check results display |
| **`components/AdminConfig.svelte`** | BYOM credential setup form (OpenAI/Anthropic API key upload) |
| **`components/WorkflowConfigPanel.svelte`** | JSON workflow config textarea + validation |
| **`components/StatusBar.svelte`** | Renders per-integration health indicators (latency, errors) |
| **`components/ChatPanel.svelte`** | Agent chat interface (not yet implemented, Epic 3) |
| **`lib/api.ts`** | Typed HTTP client (apiFetch) with 10s timeout, error envelope parsing, ApiError class |
| **`lib/tableau.ts`** | Tableau runtime wrapper (initializeExtension, getTableauUserId) with graceful fallback |

**Tech: Svelte 5 runes (`$state`), TypeScript strict, Vite 5, @tableau/extensions-api-types**

---

#### **Backend (autom9-backend)**

##### **Config Layer** (`app/config/`)
- **`workflow_registry.py`** — In-memory singleton holding active workflow config. Loaded from DB at startup; atomically updated on config upload. Provides `get_tool_definitions()` and `active_config` property.
- **`workflow_schema.py`** — Pydantic validation for JSON workflow config (semver, workflow_id, tools, agent_instructions, data_panel). Enforces non-blank fields and tool structure.

##### **Agent Layer** (`app/agent/`)
- **`provider.py`** — `LLMProvider` ABC (abstract): defines `complete(messages, tools)` and `stream()` (NotImplementedError in v1). Returns `LLMResponse(content, tool_calls, finish_reason)`.
- **`provider_factory.py`** — `get_provider()` resolves active LLM provider from DB credentials (OpenAI or Anthropic), decrypts API key, instantiates provider class. Supports provider switching without restart.
- **`openai_provider.py`** / **`anthropic_provider.py`** — Concrete provider implementations (interface set, implementations pending Story 2.3).
- **`masking.py`** — **CRITICAL**: Token-based PII masking/rehydration pipeline. `TokenMap` class maintains bidirectional mapping (token ↔ real value, session-scoped, in-memory only). Functions: `mask_fields()`, `mask_text()`, `rehydrate_text()`. Category inference from field names (consultant, client, engagement, generic). 100% branch coverage hard gate (ARC-9).

##### **Integration Layer** (`app/integrations/`)
- **`base.py`** — `IntegrationBase` ABC: defines `health_check()` (never raises, returns `IntegrationStatus`) and `execute(action, params)` (raises `IntegrationError` on failure). Isolation guarantee: one failed check does not block others.
- **`smartsheet.py`** — Submits planning requests (action: `submit_planning_request`). Column mapping cache with double-checked locking. Validates sheet/token config before execution.
- **`google_calendar.py`** / **`google_docs.py`** / **`tableau_data.py`** — Stub implementations (health checks present; execute not yet wired, Story 2.4).
- **`__init__.py`** — Exports `ALL_INTEGRATIONS` list (singleton instances).

##### **API Layer** (`app/api/`)
- **`sessions.py`** — `POST /api/sessions`: Creates session tied to Tableau user (session_id UUID, tableau_user_id).
- **`status.py`** — `GET /api/status`: Runs parallel health checks (asyncio.gather) with 5s timeout per check. Returns per-integration latency and error details. Logs all results (masked, no credentials).
- **`admin/credentials.py`** — `POST /api/admin/credentials` (auth: X-Autom9-Token header): Upsert BYOM API key (Fernet-encrypted). `GET /api/admin/credentials/{provider}`: Returns masked status.
- **`admin/config.py`** — `POST /api/admin/config` (auth: X-Autom9-Token): Upload JSON workflow config. Validates schema, deactivates old configs, saves to DB, updates in-memory registry.
- **`config.py`** — `GET /api/config/workflow`: Public endpoint. Returns active workflow config (tools, instructions, data_panel).
- **`chat.py`** — `POST /api/chat`: Primary agent endpoint. Two modes: (1) normal turn (mask input → LLM call → mask output) or (2) confirm turn (execute tool → LLM final response). Logs masked interactions to `InteractionLog`.
- **`admin/logs.py`** / **`data.py`** / **`integrations.py`** — Stub routers for future endpoints (Epic 3, Story 2.5).
- **`deps.py`** — `require_admin()` dependency: validates X-Autom9-Token header.

##### **Models Layer** (`app/models/`)
- **`session.py`** — `Session(session_id UUID, tableau_user_id, started_at)`. Maps to `sessions` table.
- **`credential_store.py`** — `CredentialStore(org_id, provider, encrypted_key, is_active, loaded_at)`. Org-level (v1), group-level scoped in v2. Fernet encryption at rest.
- **`workflow_config.py`** — `WorkflowConfig(version, config_json, is_active, loaded_at)`. Raw JSON stored; schema validation in registry.
- **`interaction_log.py`** — `InteractionLog(session_id FK, masked_input, masked_output, tool_calls, latency_ms)`. Logs only masked data (NFR7).

##### **Database & Encryption**
- **`db/engine.py`** — Async SQLAlchemy engine + session factory (asyncpg driver, PostgreSQL).
- **`db/base.py`** — `DeclarativeBase` with naming conventions.
- **`db/deps.py`** — `get_db()`: FastAPI dependency. Owns commit/rollback; routers use flush() only.
- **`services/encryption.py`** — Fernet symmetric encryption (lazy singleton). Never logs plaintext.
- **`alembic/`** — Migrations: initial schema (sessions, credential_store, workflow_configs, interaction_logs) + is_active column for configs.

##### **Core & Config**
- **`core/config.py`** — Pydantic settings: DATABASE_URL, ENCRYPTION_KEY, BACKEND_SECRET, LOG_LEVEL, CORS_ORIGINS, pool sizes, Smartsheet/Google/Tableau credentials. Fails fast on missing env vars.
- **`core/exceptions.py`** — `IntegrationError`, `ProviderError`, `MaskingError`. Custom exception handlers in `main.py` return consistent error envelope.

---

### 4. **How the Pieces Fit Together**

#### **Data Flow: Extension Load → Session Creation → Status Check**

1. **Extension mounted** → `App.svelte` onMount triggered
2. **Tableau runtime initialized** → `initializeExtension()` waits for Tableau API
3. **Tableau user extracted** → `getTableauUserId()` (or fallback in dev)
4. **Backend session created** → `POST /api/sessions` with tableau_user_id → returns session_id
5. **Session stored** → `sessionStore.sessionId = ...` (frontend state)
6. **Health checks triggered** → `GET /api/status` with X-Autom9-Session header
7. **Integration checks run in parallel** → asyncio.gather with 5s timeout per check
8. **Results rendered** → `StatusBar` displays per-integration status
9. **Admin config panel optional** → If `?admin` in URL, render `AdminConfig` and `WorkflowConfigPanel`

#### **Data Flow: Admin Configures BYOM Credentials**

1. **Admin opens extension URL with `?admin` query param**
2. **Admin selects provider** (OpenAI or Anthropic) in `AdminConfig.svelte`
3. **Admin pastes API key** → `POST /api/admin/credentials` with X-Autom9-Token header
4. **Backend validates key format** → Encrypts with Fernet → Stores in `credential_store` table
5. **Provider becomes active** → `get_provider()` queries DB and instantiates provider on next chat call
6. **Provider switching** → No app restart needed; queries DB on every chat call (FR28)

#### **Data Flow: Admin Uploads Workflow Config**

1. **Admin pastes JSON workflow config** in `WorkflowConfigPanel.svelte`
2. **Client-side parse validates JSON** → Immediate feedback on malformed input
3. **Config sent** → `POST /api/admin/config` with X-Autom9-Token header, raw JSON body
4. **Backend validates schema** → `WorkflowConfigSchema` Pydantic model (semver, tool names, agent_instructions)
5. **Old configs deactivated** → `UPDATE workflow_config SET is_active = FALSE`
6. **New config persisted** → Inserted as is_active = TRUE, flushed to DB
7. **In-memory registry updated** → `workflow_registry._active = config`
8. **Extension fetches on load** → `GET /api/config/workflow` → receives active tools & instructions

#### **Data Flow: Consultant Submits Chat Message**

1. **Consultant types message** in `ChatPanel` → sends to `/api/chat` endpoint
2. **Backend receives message** + session_context (planning data, task list, etc.)
3. **Masking pipeline starts** (ARC-9):
   - Fields in session_context registered to TokenMap → real values replaced with tokens (e.g., "CONSULTANT_001")
   - Message text scanned for registered values → longest-match-first replacement
   - Masked input logged (real values never leave frontend or appear in logs)
4. **LLM call placed** → `provider.complete(messages, tools)` with masked context
5. **LLM response arrives** → contains tool_call proposals (e.g., `{"tool": "smartsheet", "params": {...}}`)
6. **Rehydration pipeline** → Masked tokens in response replaced with real values from TokenMap
7. **Response returned to frontend** with pending_action (if tool calls present) or final text reply
8. **Consultant reviews** action proposal → clicks confirm or cancel
9. **On confirm** → `POST /api/chat` with confirm_action → orchestrator calls `_INTEGRATION_REGISTRY[integration_name].execute(action, params)`
10. **Tool execution completes** → LLM generates final "success" response → returned to frontend

---

### 5. **Notable Patterns & Tech Stack Choices**

#### **Architectural Patterns**

| Pattern | Implementation | Rationale |
|---------|---|---|
| **Integration Registry** | Dict mapping integration name → IntegrationBase instance in `chat.py` | Zero if/else in orchestration; extensible for new integrations |
| **Workflow as Config** | JSON schema + Pydantic validation; no code changes for new workflows | Core extensibility thesis (FR26–FR27) |
| **Token-Based Data Masking** | SessionStore holds TokenMap; bidirectional token↔real mapping | Balances LLM reasoning quality with enterprise PII requirements |
| **In-Memory Workflow Registry** | Loaded at startup, updated atomically on config upload | Fast access; no DB query per agent turn |
| **Org-Level Credentials** (v1) | All consultants share credentials; group-scoped in v2 | Simpler for POC; supports future multi-tenant isolation |
| **Parallel Integration Checks** | `asyncio.gather` with per-check timeout + return_exceptions | Isolation guarantee; one failure doesn't block others |
| **Fluent Async Lifecycle** | FastAPI lifespan context manager for startup tasks | Load workflow config from DB before app serves requests |

#### **Tech Stack**

**Frontend:**
- **Svelte 5** with runes (`$state`) — modern reactivity without legacy store API
- **TypeScript strict** — no implicit any
- **Vite 8** — fast dev server and production build
- **@tableau/extensions-api-types** — Tableau runtime typing

**Backend:**
- **FastAPI + Uvicorn** — async-first, auto OpenAPI docs
- **SQLAlchemy 2.0 async ORM** — asyncpg driver for PostgreSQL
- **Pydantic v2** — validation + settings management
- **Cryptography (Fernet)** — symmetric encryption for credentials at rest
- **uv** — Python package manager (faster, more reliable than pip)
- **Alembic** — database migrations (semver-style versions)
- **pytest + pytest-asyncio** — real DB testing with savepoint-based isolation
- **pythonjsonlogger** — structured JSON logs (no secrets logged)

#### **Security & Privacy Patterns**

| Feature | Implementation |
|---------|---|
| **PII Masking (FR17–FR18)** | TokenMap: session-scoped, in-memory, bidirectional token↔real mapping. Never persisted. |
| **Credential Encryption** | Fernet symmetric encryption; keys stored in env var (never logged). |
| **No Credential Exposure** | Logs masked only; UI hides raw keys; config files never contain secrets. |
| **Integration Isolation** | One failed integration doesn't cascade; health checks have per-check timeouts. |
| **Admin Auth** | X-Autom9-Token header (BACKEND_SECRET env var); not automatically injected by frontend (v1 concern). |

#### **Notable Decisions**

- **Chat endpoint supports two modes** (normal + confirm) to enable action review workflow (FR6: "Consultant can review before execution").
- **Integration registry is a zero-if/else dict lookup** — makes adding new integrations trivial.
- **Masking category inferred from field names** (e.g., "consultant_name" → category "consultant") — removes config burden.
- **Longest-match-first replacement in mask_text()** — prevents partial substitutions (e.g., "Acme Corp" masked before "Acme").
- **Status checks run in parallel with asyncio.gather** — scales to many integrations without sequential latency.
- **Workflow config persisted as raw JSON** — schema validation in registry, not in DB, preserves schema evolution flexibility.

---

### **Summary**

**autom9** is a **two-tier BYOM agentic BI extension**:
- **Frontend (Svelte)** inside Tableau, handling session lifecycle, status display, and admin config
- **Backend (FastAPI)** orchestrating LLM calls, integration execution, token masking/rehydration, and workflow configuration
- **Data flows** through a masking pipeline to ensure PII never reaches external LLM providers
- **Integration registry** enables zero-code addition of new tool actions
- **JSON workflow configuration** with Pydantic schema validation enables extensibility without code changes
- **Parallel health checks** with per-check timeouts ensure one failure doesn't block the system
- **Async throughout** (Svelte async + FastAPI async ORM) for responsive, scalable performance

The architecture is explicitly designed to **validate the platform thesis** (extensibility via config, not code) and **support future self-hosted and local-LLM deployments** without architectural rework.
